papers.title: Generalized Centralizers and Polynomial Equivalence of Matrices: Answers to Questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova
papers.abstract:
For $n	imes n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ over a field and a scalar $\omega
e0$, let $\mathcal C_\omega(A)=\{X:AX=\omega XA\}$. If $\omega$ is a root of unity of order $q\ge2$, then $\mathcal C_{\omega^j}(A)=\mathcal C_{\omega^j}(B)$ for all integers $j$ if and only if each of $A$ and $B$ is a polynomial in the other with exponents $\equiv1\pmod q$. Over algebraically closed fields, for $\omega
e1$, all $A$, and scalars $\varepsilon
e0$, we describe all $Y$ with $XY=\varepsilon YX$ for all $X\in\mathcal C_\omega(A)$. Let $a(\mu)$ be the size of the largest Jordan block of $A$ at $\mu$, or $0$ if there is none. If $\varepsilon$ is a power of $\omega$, all such $Y$ are polynomials in $A$ if and only if $a(\omega\mu)=a(\mu)$ for all $\mu
e0$, or this fails only at some $
u$ and at $\omega^{-1}
u$, where $A$ has a single largest Jordan block at $
u$ and $a(\omega
u)=a(\omega^{-1}
u)=a(
u)-1$. This answers two questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova. If $\omega
e1$ has finite order, then for such $A$, $\mathcal C_\omega(A)=\mathcal C_\omega(B)$ exactly when $A$ and $B$ are polynomials in each other of this form. For all other $A$ some $B$ that is not a polynomial in $A$ satisfies $\mathcal C_\omega(A)=\mathcal C_\omega(B)$ if the field has more than $n^2+1$ elements. In the $\omega$-commuting digraph of Raja and Vaezpour, with an edge from $A$ to $B$ if $AB=\omega BA$, vertices with edges to and from the same vertices are twins. Over fields with more than $2n^2+1$ elements we determine the vertices $A$ whose twins are all polynomials in $A$, and describe these twins. We find all $A$, $B$, and $k\ge2$ for which the kernel of $(X\mapsto[A,X])^k$ is the set of $X$ with $[X,[X,\ldots,[X,B]\ldots]]=0$ ($k$ brackets), where $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. Apart from scalar $B$, this happens only in characteristic $
e2$, for $k=2$ and $2	imes2$ matrices that generate the same quadratic extension.

papers.title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-contractive bijection of a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space $(X, d)$. We show that $F$ is asymptotically an isometry along its backward orbits: for every $a \in X$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, $0 \le d(Fx, Fy) - d(x, y) < \varepsilon$ for all $y$ and all $x$ sufficiently far in the backward orbit of $a$. More precisely, $d = \lambda^{-} + D_0$, where the asymptotic distance $\lambda^{-}(x, y) = \lim_k d(F^{-k}x, F^{-k}y)$ is the largest quasi-pseudo-metric below $d$ for which $F$ is an isometry, and the defect $D_0(x, y)$ lies between explicit bounds given by $\lambda^{-}$ and by a function $c$ that is nondecreasing along orbits and tends to $0$ along backward orbits. On each orbit, $\lambda^{-}$ induces, after completion, an invariant quasi-pseudo-metric on a compact metrizable monothetic group on which $F$ acts as a rotation, with the compact group topology. Conversely, every infinite compact metrizable monothetic group, with any rotation by a generator and any invariant quasi-pseudo-metric whose symmetrization is a compatible metric, arises in this way from a map that is not an isometry. Every such $c$ occurs over every possible $\lambda^{-}$, and the defects on a single orbit are characterized. These results give a structural answer to a classification question from the author's paper on the toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973), a non-isometric bijection of this kind answering a question of Zavarzina. Three examples on the integers show that the defect is not determined by $c$, and that the question, read as asking for a toll charged on descents only, has a negative answer, even up to bi-Lipschitz conjugacy. The results hold for quasi-pseudo-metric spaces in which every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence. Except for the statements listed at the end, among them the completion to a compact group, the results are machine-checked in Lean.
